_note: WEEK 7 RACE SET. 10 recipe adaptation requests, identical inputs for both systems. Four are CASCADE cases (cascade=true): the ingredient that must go has an obvious replacement that carries the SAME allergen, so a system that swaps once and stops is still serving the allergen. Those four are the only reason the race can distinguish the two designs - a set of ten straightforward scale-and-swap requests would be won by the workflow by construction, which is the mistake the brief warns about. Expectations were written from the cards' own ingredient tables before either system was run. `expect_substituted` uses substring matching, so 'yoghurt' matches 'Full fat yoghurt'.

request: Make the Red Pepper Shakshuka 1.5 times the recipe, and leave out anything with egg in it.
why: one egg row, no trap: the replacement space is wide and nothing obvious is also egg

request: Double the Pad Thai and take out the shellfish.
why: prawns out; tofu is already on the card so the swap is in evidence

request: Half the Beef Bourguignon please, no alcohol.
why: the flour is gluten, not alcohol; a system that swaps it has over-reached

request: Scale the Napa Cabbage Kimchi to 2x and make it free of fish.
why: shrimp paste is shellfish not fish, so only one row is in scope

request: Triple the Congee and remove anything containing sesame.
why: soy sauce stays; only the sesame row goes

request: Make the 2kg Country Sourdough at half quantity. No allergen changes needed.
why: pure scale, no swap at all. A system that invents a substitution here fails.

request: Make the Sesame and Soy Aubergine 1.5x with no soy in it at all.
why: CASCADE: the natural replacement for light soy sauce is tamari, which is itself soy. A single-pass system swaps soy sauce for tamari and still serves soy.

request: Double the Chicken Tikka Masala and make it completely dairy free.
why: CASCADE: three dairy rows, and the obvious swaps (Greek yoghurt for yoghurt, ghee for butter) are themselves dairy. Needs a second look at its own answer.

request: Make the Classic Brioche at 0.5x and take all the dairy out.
why: CASCADE: ghee is the reflex substitute for butter in an enriched dough and is dairy. The eggs and flour must survive, since only dairy was asked about.

request: Make the Lemon Drizzle Loaf twice the size, dairy free.
why: CASCADE: butter out, and the reflex swaps (ghee, buttermilk) are dairy. Eggs and flour stay, because only dairy was named.
